title: A familiar thing gets a look when someone names it, by 15 months
summary: CDC says that by 15 months most children look at a familiar object when a person names it.
body: The 15-month CDC sheet has a comprehension entry that is only about looking. When a familiar object is named, the child looks at it. The entry does not ask for a pronunciation, and it does not say how large the set of known object names is. A cup, a shoe, or a pet could be the object. The sheet does not pick one. This looking entry is a United States group mark. It is not an eye exam, and it is not a score for any single child.
